when.quote: Use this process when a customer believes there is a discrepancy between the cash back they received for a particular transaction and the cash back they should have received. This process applies to all credit card transactions.

info.about: Something to find the customer's record with: full name, email or user id
info.ask: Could you please give me your full name so I can find your profile?

info.about: Any 2 of: date of birth, email, phone number, address. They must match the record.
info.ask: To verify your identity, could you please give me two of these: your date of birth, email, phone number or address on file?

info.about: The customer's user id from the lookup. The customer passes it to the dispute tool.
The customer's cards and card types, used to find each transaction's earn rate
Each transaction's transaction_id, card type, merchant, amount, category and rewards_earned
Transactions whose recorded rewards differ from the recalculated value. The customer may not know them; the agent finds them in the records.

steps.do: Greet the customer and ask what they need
Ask for the customer's name and 2 of: DOB, email, phone, address
steps.quote: ensure that they are able to give correctly any 2 out of the following values: date of birth, email, phone number, address

args.customer_name: the name the customer gave (or use get_user_information_by_email / _by_id)

steps.quote: To verify the identity of the user, call the appropriate read tools

steps.do: Check that 2 of the values match the record; if they do not, stop and share no account details
steps.quote: Do not leak any information about the user before they are verified.

steps.do: Get the current time for the verification log
steps.quote: If you need the current time, always use the get_current_time() tool.
After verification, you must call the verification logging tool to properly log the information into the verification records.

steps.do: Get the customer's credit card accounts
steps.quote: Our customer service team has the tools to investigate cash back discrepancies and review your transaction history.

steps.do: Get the customer's credit card transactions
steps.quote: When you contact us, we'll look into the specific transaction, verify the merchant category, check the applicable reward rates for your card, and determine if an adjustment is needed.

steps.do: For each transaction, work out the correct points from the card's rate, the merchant/category, the exclusions and any promotion, rounding down. Compare the result with the recorded rewards_earned and list the transactions that do not match.
steps.quote: Recalculate the correct rewards for each transaction based on the card type, transaction category, and any applicable promotions.

steps.do: Tell the customer which transactions (transaction_ids) earned the wrong rewards and what they should have earned. If none are wrong, explain the rates and close.
steps.quote: Confirm the customer has the correct transaction_id before they submit.

steps.do: Give the customer the cash back dispute tool
steps.if: at least one transaction's recorded rewards differ from the recalculated value
steps.quote: Tool to provide to the user: `submit_cash_back_dispute_0589(user_id: str, transaction_id: str)`

steps.do: Tell the customer to run the tool once for each wrong transaction, using their user_id and that transaction_id. Mention that supporting context may be requested later during review.
steps.quote: Tell the customer to run the tool with their own user_id and the specific transaction_id for the purchase in question.

steps.do: Submit a cash back dispute for each wrong transaction
steps.quote: the submission itself is initiated with the tool above.

steps.if: the dispute is resolved and approved
steps.quote: Use `unlock_discoverable_agent_tool` to unlock the agent tool `update_transaction_rewards_3847`.

steps.do: Set each disputed transaction's rewards to the recalculated value, formatted as 'X points'
steps.if: the dispute is resolved and approved
steps.quote: new_rewards_earned: a string formatted as 'X points' where X is the correct whole-number point value

steps.do: Re-read the transactions to confirm the corrected rewards
steps.quote: Confirm the update in credit_card_transaction_history after the tool call completes.

rules.rule: Rewards are stored as points; for cash back cards, 1 point = $0.01. So points = purchase amount × cash back % × 100 (2.5% gives 2.5 points per dollar).
rules.quote: these 'points' should be interpreted as cash back with a conversion rate of 1 point = $0.01

rules.rule: Gold Rewards Card earns 2.5% cash back on all purchases (2.5 points per dollar).
EcoCard earns 5 points per dollar on green purchases and 1 point per dollar on other purchases.
rules.quote: The only true points-based card is the EcoCard, which earns 'sustainability points' (5 points per dollar on green purchases, 1 point per dollar on other purchases)

rules.rule: EcoCard green categories include public transit, EV charging, renewable energy, certified sustainable retailers/eco-labeled products, and bike share/micromobility.
EcoCard purchases at Target, Walmart, Amazon or ThredUp earn only 1 point per dollar, even for eco products.
rules.quote: Buying eco-labeled or “sustainable” items from the excluded general retailers still earns the standard rate.

rules.rule: EcoCard EV charging earns 5x only at Tesla Supercharger, ChargePoint or EVgo; other networks earn 1x.
rules.quote: EV charging only qualifies for green rewards when using one of our 3 certified partner charging networks: Tesla Supercharger, ChargePoint, or EVgo. Charging at any other network does not qualify.

rules.rule: Always round points down (floor) to a whole number.
rules.quote: All credit card rewards points are rounded down to the nearest whole number.

rules.rule: Do not trust an expected_rewards value; verify the rates yourself.
rules.quote: Important: Do not rely on any expected_rewards field in the dispute record. Independently verify rates and eligibility.

rules.rule: Do not ask for card numbers or other sensitive card details.
rules.quote: Do not collect sensitive card details; the tool uses the identifiers provided by the user.

rules.rule: Apply any active promotion or bonus category in force at the time of purchase (none was found for Gold Rewards Card; the EcoCard promos are a new-customer signup bonus and an APR offer, not per-transaction earn rates).
rules.quote: Ensure your calculation reflects the proper base rate and any active bonus category or promotion at the time of purchase.

jobs.done_when: The customer is verified and logged. Every transaction has been checked against its correct rewards. The customer has the submit_cash_back_dispute_0589 tool and has submitted a dispute for each wrong transaction. If a dispute came back resolved and approved, its corrected points were applied with update_transaction_rewards_3847 and confirmed in the transaction history.

documents.why: Cash back dispute procedure; the customer-run tool submit_cash_back_dispute_0589
How to apply corrections for resolved disputes with update_transaction_rewards_3847; recalculation rules
Rewards stored as points; 1 point = $0.01; EcoCard earns 5/1 points per dollar
What a cash back investigation involves: transaction, merchant category, card rates
Gold Rewards Card 2.5% cash back on all purchases
EcoCard earn rates for green and other purchases
Which EcoCard purchases count as green
EcoCard exclusions (Target, Walmart, Amazon, ThredUp) and EV charging networks

open_questions: The documents do not say how a submission becomes 'resolved and approved', and the agent has no tool to read the cash_back_disputes database. The agent should apply update_transaction_rewards_3847 only if the submission result or records show the dispute was approved.
The documents do not map transaction category values to EcoCard 'green'. The agent must judge from the category and merchant name against the green list and exclusions.
The documents do not say whether to compute points from the exact amount (floor(amount × rate)) or from whole dollars. The rounding examples suggest floor(amount × points-per-dollar).
